title: Bracket Check
statement: A configuration file uses three kinds of brackets: round `()`, square `[]` and curly `{}`. Before the file is loaded, a checker confirms that the brackets are balanced.
A string is balanced when every opening bracket is closed by the same kind of bracket, brackets close in the reverse order they were opened, and no closing bracket appears without a matching opener.
inputFormat: A single line containing a nonempty string made only of the characters `()[]{}`.
outputFormat: Print `YES` if the string is balanced, otherwise print `NO`.
constraints: Nesting can be up to 100000 levels deep, so avoid recursion that uses one call per bracket.

examples.explanation: Each bracket closes in reverse order of opening.
A round bracket is closed by a square bracket.

input: Line 1: a string s made of the characters ()[]{}

private.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space with an explicit stack.
private.notes: Odd length strings are always NO. A leftover opener at the end is NO.
